Interview GPS vs. reported home location

Two independent checks on one map. Marker fill color is the village-level check: is this GPS point close to where other respondents who reported the same town/village landed? Marker border is the district-level check: does this respondent's reported home district actually contain their GPS point, using official Uganda district boundaries -- this catches gross location errors even when there's no one else in the same village to compare against. A black border is a strong signal (mismatched into a non-neighboring district); an orange border usually just means the GPS point landed in a neighboring district (e.g. Kampala/Wakiso), which is commonly a boundary quirk rather than a real problem.

Pick an enumerator below to see only their interviews, or pick a reported location to see everyone who said they live in that town/village. Tick Flagged/OK/Not comparable to isolate one village-level status, or a district status to isolate that. Drag the distance slider to show only interviews further than a given distance from where other respondents in the same reported village/town landed (set the left handle to -1 to also include singleton/not-comparable locations). Use the layer control (top right of the map) to switch between satellite, street, and a minimal light basemap, and the fullscreen button (top left) to zoom in further.
